instantiated_cells.justification: Section 86117(a) requires reports to be filed during the month following each calendar quarter, not annually.
The statute specifies quarterly reporting (filed in the month following each calendar quarter) rather than monthly reporting.
Persons described in §86115 must file periodic reports under §86116 on the quarterly schedule in §86117(a), with no alternative frequency stated.
Reports required by §86116 are filed during the month following each calendar quarter, i.e., quarterly.
The reporting schedule is quarterly, not semi-annual.
Section 86117(a) ties filing to calendar quarters, not a tri-annual legislative-calendar schedule.
Lobbyist employer registration must include information identifying the filer's nature and interests, including a description of the business activity in which it is engaged.
Periodic reports must disclose total payments to each lobbying firm and total payments to lobbyists employed by the filer, capturing compensation costs.
Section 86116 lists required contents (payments, activity expenses, interests, contributions, etc.) but does not require disclosure of specific lobbying contacts/communications.
The periodic report must include a description of the filer's specific lobbying interests, which constitutes disclosure of general issues lobbied.
Filers must report each activity expense, and activity expenses include gifts and other benefits to officials, with required details such as date, amount, beneficiary, and payee.

The report must include the total of all other payments to influence legislative or administrative action, including overhead expenses and certain employee costs, i.e., indirect non-compensation costs.
The statute requires reporting total payments to each lobbying firm but does not require disclosing the contracted lobbyists' addresses and phone numbers in the periodic spending report.

Section 86116 does not require listing names of all lobbyists representing the filer (it requires payments to firms/lobbyists and includes lobbyists' periodic reports only for employed lobbyists under §86116(e)).
No provision in §86116 requires disclosure of the principal's major financial contributors.
The periodic report must state the filer's name, business address, and telephone number.
The statute calls for a description of specific lobbying interests but does not require listing specific bill numbers or legislation IDs.

The report aggregates total payments to lobbying firms, total payments to employed lobbyists, and the total of all other payments to influence legislative/administrative action, together capturing total lobbying expenditures.

The principal's periodic report must report total amounts paid to each lobbying firm and total amounts paid to lobbyists employed by the filer, thereby including salary/fees paid to lobbyist(s) as spending amounts.
Reports must itemize payments by lobbying firm (total to each firm) and itemize each activity expense by date, amount, beneficiary, and payee rather than only a single lump-sum.
Section 86116 requires reporting payments, expenses, lobbying interests, and contributions but does not require listing all sponsors or members of associations/representative groups.
A lobbyist employer's periodic report must include a periodic report completed and verified by each lobbyist employed by the employer, effectively identifying the lobbyists employed by the filer.
